name: deck-properties
body:
A `kalide.yaml` deck may declare a `properties:` block of author-chosen deck-wide key/value pairs, readable from every slide layout and every section template (template-context). Keys are arbitrary non-empty strings chosen by the author; inside `properties:` they are not subject to the top-level unknown-key rule (only the `properties` key itself is a recognised top-level key, deck-config). Values are simple typed YAML scalars only — a string, a number, a boolean, or a date written `YYYY-MM-DD`; a mapping or a sequence as a value is a config error naming the key. Values reach templates as typed values, exactly as fields do: a string is a plain html/template-escaped string (never Markdown, never pre-rendered safe HTML); a number, boolean or date is the corresponding typed value, not a display string. An absent or empty `properties:` block is allowed and contributes no properties.
AC: a deck with `properties: {audience: engineers, fiscal-year: 2026, confidential: true, kickoff: 2026-09-27}` loads and each value is readable from a slide layout and a section template; a mapping or sequence value (e.g. `properties: {tags: [a, b]}`) is a config error naming the key; an unknown top-level key other than title/author/date/theme/navigation/properties still errors with a closest-match suggestion.
